mark_split.label: Apply the property and simplify tan(π/4 − θ)

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Senior Inter Maths-2B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book printed p.42 (PDF page 41) — LAQ chapter 4 'Definite Integrals', answer 36.2, the right-hand twin of answer 36.1 on the same printed Super Scoring Page (SSP 42). The book's own printed note calls the pair 'SUPER TWIN BABIES' and states 'AFTER SIMPLIFICATION BABY 2 BECOMES SAME AS BABY 1' — verified independently here by the x = tanθ substitution, which turns this integral into exactly answer 36.1's ∫₀^(π/4) log(1+tanθ)dθ. Printed appearance: AP 18, 22 and TS 17, 19, plus a third year at the scan's right edge that is cropped and not legibly recorded. Chapter star rank ★★★ applies. No margin mark tags are printed on this page, so the 2+3+2 split is OURS, weighting the tan(A−B) algebra block at 3 marks the same way as its twin (ts_ipe_m2b_di_laq_log_1plus_tanx_0_to_pi4), patterned on the same book p.17 1+1+1+4 precedent. Boundary reading: printed p.37 (PDF 36) and printed p.44 (PDF 44) confirm the chapter span. No two-book union check and no board back-test were possible for Maths-2B (no second-year TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand; the book's five Guess Papers pp.118-127 stand in for the back-test). This integral is re-answered on the Bullet Model Paper (book p.116) in the identical 'or' form alongside answer 36.1 — no separate card is authored for that appearance.

insider_note: The x = tanθ substitution is the key step: once it is made, this question becomes word-for-word the previous one. Recognising the twin saves re-deriving the tan(A−B) algebra from scratch.

steps.label: Substitute x = tanθ
steps.margin_note: First two marks. 1 + x² becomes sec²θ, which cancels the sec²θ dθ from dx exactly.
steps.memory_tip: x = tanθ is the standard substitution whenever 1 + x² sits in a denominator.
lines: Put x = tanθ ⇒ dx = sec²θ dθ. x = 0 ⇒ θ = 0; x = 1 ⇒ θ = π/4
∴ I = ∫₀^1 log(1 + x)/(1 + x²) dx = ∫₀^(π/4) log(1 + tanθ)/sec²θ · sec²θ dθ
steps.why: x = tanθ turns 1 + x² into sec²θ, which exactly cancels the sec²θ that comes from dx — the whole denominator vanishes, leaving a plain log(1+tanθ) integral in the new variable θ.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to change the limits from x = 0, 1 to θ = 0, π/4.
Not cancelling the sec²θ from the numerator (dx) with the sec²θ in the denominator (1+x²).

steps.label: Apply the property and simplify tan(π/4 − θ)
steps.margin_note: Three marks — the same algebra as the previous question, now with θ in place of x.
steps.memory_tip: tan(π/4 − θ) = (1 − tanθ)/(1 + tanθ) — the identical identity as the previous question.
lines: By θ → π/4 − θ: I = ∫₀^(π/4) log[1 + tan(π/4 − θ)] dθ
steps.why: Once the integral is written in θ it is identical in form to the previous question's integral, so the same tan(A−B) reduction applies unchanged.
common_mistakes: Re-deriving the algebra with the wrong variable name and losing track of which step is which.
Skipping the log-splitting step log[2/(1+tanθ)] = log2 − log(1+tanθ).

steps.label: Solve for I
steps.margin_note: The last two marks. Same final arithmetic as the previous question.
steps.memory_tip: Add I to both sides of I = (π/4)log2 − I to get 2I = (π/4)log2.
steps.why: Adding I to both sides gives 2I directly, and dividing by 2 gives the same final value as the twin question — confirming the book's claim that the two integrals are equal.
common_mistakes: Reporting a different numeric value from the twin question 36.1 without checking the arithmetic — both must agree.
